GitHub Setup

This project is hosted at https://github.com/ulenarofmondarth/pdt. It is licensed under the MIT License which allows you to pretty much do as you like with this code.

Tip

I recommend you create a fork of this repository if you intend to modify the source code.

Workflows

There are two main scenarios for automated workflows. Both start with a user commiting to main.

Initial responses

Two workflows may respond immediately:

  1. bump-version

    This will check if the pushed commits require an update to the project’s version. If they do, then various ‘version’ entries in configuration files are updated, the project is then committed back with these updated files and tagged with a new version tag (this triggers the other scenario below).

  2. build-and-deploy-docs

    If only files under docs/ are affected by the commits in this push, the documentation is rebuilt and deployed.

    This scenarion assumes that any documentation only changes remain relevant to the current version of the application.

Follow-up responses

If a version bump (bump-version) was executed then another push will occur. This push will be associated with a tag for the new release and this triggers:

  • build-on-push

    If the push it tagged (and affects files outside docs/—it should if it were bumped), this builds the application and publishes it to npmjs. It also builds and deploys the documentation.
